links.claim: Not today: an XRPL escrow can hold official RLUSD only after its issuer enables AllowTrustLineLocking, and the RLUSD issuer had not enabled it on Mainnet or Testnet when the team checked on 11 November 2026. The TokenEscrow amendment (XLS-85), which lets an escrow hold issued tokens, is already enabled on both networks, so the issuer flag is the remaining blocker. Only the issuer can set that flag, with an AccountSet transaction; a buyer or writer cannot set it for them.

links.claim: Build note, TEST-SGD stand-in: our alternative is TEST-SGD, an IOU issued by our own Testnet issuer with no real value. It stands in for RLUSD in a mechanism experiment; it is neither official RLUSD nor evidence of stablecoin adoption. S$ prices map 1:1 to TEST-SGD; this is neither a peg nor a backing claim. The experimental issuer enables token locking before the buyer and writer establish eligible trust lines. A successful TEST-SGD escrow proves only that this configured stand-in worked on Testnet; it does not change the official RLUSD issuer's permissions or establish a live bank settlement partnership. Sources accessed 11 November 2026.
